CURRENT RELEASE · CONTROLLED AUTO-EVENTING

39 of 40 events found. In a controlled fixture.

The frozen shipping detector matched 39 of 40 expected events across five previously unused procedural seeds: 97.5% recall and 100% precision inside this study. The low-light miss remains in the published result.

This uses a fixed camera, known pitch calibration, enrolled colour markers and a visible ball. It is not validation on moving-camera professional broadcast footage or unmarked players.

HUMAN RATINGS PENDING

Let people judge the commentary.

The current model-scored court tests six preregistered synthetic cases in four blinded passes with reversed A/B order. Its 94–90 result is narrow evidence, not independent human preference.

The blind review keeps ratings on each reviewer’s device until export. Equal scores are valid; no generated judge counts as an independent person.

CURRENT DETECTOR / FROZEN BEFORE HOLDOUT

What did automatic eventing establish?

Loading current holdout…

The detector consumes decoded pixels and emits candidate passes, shots, identities, distances and speeds. Ground truth is visible only to the evaluator. The result establishes controlled synthetic performance for this exact source hash; it does not establish broadcast-match accuracy.

What happens outside the controlled fixture?

Loading retained results…

CINEMATIC COMPANION / SEPARATE PROVENANCE

The film communicates the story. It does not supply the measurements.

The current 1:53 judge demo uses an edited minute made from eight independently generated shots. Character and ball continuity can vary between cuts. It is labelled as fictional companion film and is not presented as one continuously observed play.

BTR’s measurements come from the separately labelled synthetic event and tracking records. A fully measured, photoreal, continuous 22-player match remains future work.

What would close the remaining gaps?

Broadcast validation: freeze the detector, independently annotate unfamiliar licensed match clips with moving cameras, occlusion and varied kits, then publish misses and false events.

Continuous measured film: render licensed realistic characters from the frozen tracking pack, preserve identity and contact through every frame, and retain camera calibration.

Commentary: collect complete blind ratings from people who did not build BTR and publish the result even if the baseline wins.
